text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zambian press on Tuesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Ten managers at the privately-owned Credit Africa Bank have been sacked for alleged fraud.
- The civil servants' union says it will oppose government plans to send over 3,000 agriculture ministry workers on forced leave as they wait to be redeployed or given lay-off packages.
- The Zambia Congress of Trade Unions has formed a committee to monitor trade union activites in privatised companies.
- Maamba Collieries said coal production would resume a week after repairs to the plant which was damaged by flooding last week.
- Cholera has broken out in a Lusaka prison and eight inmates have been admitted to hospital for treatment.

- The Mine Workers Union of Zambia said it would not accept the sale of Zambia Consolidated Copper Mines (ZCCM) units to companies that offered workers less attractive conditions of service than they enjoyed under ZCCM.
